about: The timestamping authorities the verifiers in this repository trust unless the reader says otherwise. An authority's root here is what lets a verifier check the `timestamp` attachment of vcap-spec §7: an RFC 3161 token that binds the proof's core hash to an instant. Without a root for the authority a token chains to, the verdict carries *trusted time not evaluated*, the validated instant falls back to the device's own clock, and nothing is lost but that one check.
how_to_replace: This document is data, not code. The page publishes it verbatim as `tsa.json` next to itself, the CLI reads this file and takes `--tsa-root <file.pem>` and `--no-default-tsa`, and every verifier here can be run against a set that does not contain any of these authorities. Verifying without them is the supported case, not a degraded one. It is a separate document from `logs.json` because it answers a separate question: refusing a log this project runs and keeping a third-party clock is a coherent position, and `--no-default-logs` and `--no-default-tsa` are therefore separate switches.
fingerprint_is: the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the DER certificate — what `openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256` prints, without the colons. Recompute it from `certificate` before trusting this file: the two fields check each other.

authorities.name: FreeTSA root CA
authorities.subject: O=Free TSA, OU=Root CA, CN=www.freetsa.org, L=Wuerzburg, ST=Bayern, C=DE
authorities.operator: freetsa.org — a free public timestamping service run by a third party, with no relationship to the vcap project
authorities.proves: that the hash in the token existed before the instant the token states, and that this authority signed that statement. A token is evidence about a hash and a clock, and about nothing else.
authorities.does_not_prove: anything about who made the file, what it shows, or where it was taken. A timestamp over a forged file is a valid timestamp over a forged file. It also does not prove the authority's clock was right — only that the authority vouched for it.
caveats: A free community service with no SLA, no contractual liability and no audited compliance regime. Nobody owes anyone an answer if it is wrong, and nobody owes anyone uptime. This is not a qualified trust service under eIDAS: a token from it has no presumption of accuracy in a European court, and a dispute would turn on what the certificate says and on nothing else.

This is the authority the platform is configured to ask today, and that is an operational choice, not a property of the format. Changing provider means a new entry here — never an edit of this one, because tokens already minted keep chaining to this root.
The root is what is pinned; the signing certificate that actually mints tokens is inside each token and chains to it. Its rotation costs this document nothing.
